# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“IT’S time Nell was in to do her sewing,” declared Thirza, looking first toward the clock and then toward the yellow August afternoon, where the heat caused everything to drowse. “She remained playing with Isolde over thirty minutes longer than I permitted her to; and at present she’s seated out there on the woodpile speaking to Obed, nineteen to the dozen, despite knowing full well that she should be doing her chores. And naturally he’s attending to her like an utter ninny. I never witnessed a man so infatuated. The further she speaks and the stranger her words become, the more pleased he appears to be. Nell Harcourt, you come right in here this minute, do you hear me!”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0000 }

Nell came rushing inside from the yard because of a succession of sharp taps against the west window, her gaze gleaming, her cheeks lightly tinged with a rose hue, and her unplaited hair flowing out after her like a radiant river.
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0001 }

“Oh, Thirza,” she cried out, gasping for air, “a Sunday-school picnic is happening next week—taking place in Mr. Gorham Pullen’s field, very close to the lake of Glassy Waters. Also, Mrs. Superintendent Bell along with Mrs. Agatha Sowerby intend to prepare ice cream—imagine that, Thirza—ice cream! And, oh, Thirza, am I allowed to attend?”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0002 }

“Nell, be so good as to check the time on the clock. At what hour did I instruct you to return?”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0003 }

“It is two o'clock—however, isn't the news regarding the picnic marvelous, Thirza? Am I allowed to go, please? Oh, a picnic is something I have never attended—picnics are things I have envisioned in my dreams, yet I have never—”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0004 }

“Indeed, I instructed you to arrive at two o'clock. Yet the time is now a quarter to three. I want an explanation for your disobedience, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0005 }

“Why, Thirza, I intended to, as fully as possible. But Larkrise is fascinating beyond what you can imagine. And besides, I needed to inform Obed regarding the picnic. Such a sympathetic listener, Obed is. May I please go?”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0006 }

“You must train yourself to withstand the attraction of Idle-whatever-its-name-is. If I order you to return at a specific hour, my intention is that exact hour, rather than thirty minutes after it. Furthermore, there is no need for you to pause and converse with understanding hearers along your path. Regarding the picnic, naturally your attendance is permitted. You attend Sunday school, so it is improbable that I would deny you permission to attend when every other young girl is attending.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0007 }

“However—however,” stammered Nell, “Isolde claims that each person is required to bring a food basket. Thirza, you are aware that I am unable to cook, and—and—I am not as bothered about attending a picnic lacking puffed sleeves, yet being forced to attend without a basket would make me feel deeply ashamed. It has been haunting my thoughts from the moment Isolde mentioned it.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0008 }

“Well, there is no need for it to weigh on your mind any further. I will prepare a basket of baked goods for you.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0009 }

“Oh, you sweet precious Thirza. Oh, you show me such kindness. Oh, I feel so deeply indebted to you.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0010 }

Finishing her “ohs,” Nell threw herself into Thirza’s arms and enthusiastically kissed her sallow cheek. Thirza’s face had never before in her entire life been willingly touched by childish lips. Once more she felt the thrill of that unexpected, astonishingly sweet sensation. Nell’s sudden embrace secretly delighted her immensely, which was likely why she remarked curtly:
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0011 }

“Now, now, forget about your affection nonsense. I would rather watch you obey my instructions precisely. Regarding culinary work, I intend to start instructing you in it one of these upcoming days. However, you are so scatterbrained, Nell, that I have postponed starting until I see whether you might settle down somewhat and become reliable. One must remain fully focused during food preparation instead of halting midway to allow one's mind to wander everywhere. Presently, fetch your needlework and finish your block prior to teatime.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0012 }

“Patchwork isn't to my liking,” Nell uttered sorrowfully, searching for her sewing basket and placing herself in front of a small pile of white and red diamond shapes while sighing. “Certain types of needlework would probably be pleasant, I believe; however, patchwork provides no room for imagination. One small seam merely follows another, and you appear to make no progress whatsoever. Still, I naturally prefer being Nell of Grey Shutters stitching patchwork over being Nell belonging to any different location with nothing else to do except play. Even so, I wish the hours passed as rapidly while stitching patches as they pass when I am playing together with Isolde. Oh, Thirza, we experience such wonderful times. I must supply the majority of the imagination, yet I am fully capable of managing that. Every other aspect of Isolde is utterly flawless. You are aware of that small plot of ground across the stream that extends upward between our property and that of Mr. Pembroke. Mr. William Bell owns it, and right inside the corner stands a small circle of white birch trees—a most romantic place, Thirza. Isolde and I maintain our playhouse at that location. Larkrise is the name we give it. Does that not sound like a poetical name? I can promise you that devising it took me a considerable amount of time. I lay awake for almost an entire night prior to creating it. Then, right as sleep was coming over me, it arrived like an inspiration. Isolde was delighted upon hearing it. Our house is arranged in an elegant fashion. Thirza, you must visit and look at it—will you not? Moss covers large stones that serve as our seats, and planks stretched between trees act as shelves. All our dishes are arranged upon them. Naturally, every piece is broken, yet imagining that they are intact is the simplest matter imaginable. One portion of a plate featuring a branch of yellow and red ivy is particularly magnificent. We store it inside the parlor, where we also keep the fairy glass. As lovely as a dream, that fairy glass is. Isolde discovered it outdoors in the forest behind their chicken coop. It is completely filled with rainbows—merely tiny young rainbows that are not yet fully grown—and Isolde's mother informed her that it had been broken away from a hanging lamp which they used to own. Nevertheless, imagining that the fairies misplaced it during a ball one night is lovely, so we name it the fairy glass. A table is going to be built for us by Obed. Oh, Reedmere is what we have called that small circular pond over inside Mr. Pembroke's field. That name came to me from the volume Isolde provided to me. Thirza, that volume was thrilling. Five lovers belonged to the heroine. A single one would satisfy me, would it not satisfy you? Very beautiful, she underwent immense suffering. Fainting was the easiest thing for her to do. Being capable of fainting is something I would adore, would you not like that, Thirza? Romantic is what it is. Yet, despite being so thin, I am actually extremely healthy. However, I think that I am becoming plumper. Do you not agree that I am? Every morning upon rising, I check my elbows to observe whether dimples are starting to form. A new dress featuring elbow sleeves is being fashioned for Isolde. She intends to wear it when attending the picnic. Oh, I truly trust the weather will be pleasant this coming Wednesday. Should something occur that hinders me from attending the picnic, I do not think I could bear the disappointment. Survival would likely happen, I suppose, but I am convinced a lifetime of grief would result. Attending one hundred picnics during future years would not count; missing this specific one could not be compensated for by them. Boats are to be present on the Lake of Glassy Waters—along with ice cream, as I previously mentioned to you. Ice cream has never been tasted by me. What it tasted like was something Isolde attempted to describe, but my guess is that ice cream belongs to those matters that lie outside imagination.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0013 }

“Nell, your speech has continued without interruption for ten minutes according to the clock,” Thirza stated. “Now, merely to satisfy my curiosity, discover whether you are able to remain silent for an equal duration of time.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0014 }

Nell remained silent as requested. However, during the remainder of the week, picnics filled her conversation, her thoughts, and her dreams. When rain fell on Saturday, she grew so terribly agitated fearing the downpour might persist up to and through Wednesday that Thirza forced her to stitch one more patchwork square to calm her nerves.
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0015 }

While returning home from church on Sunday, Nell confessed to Thirza that an actual chill of excitement swept over her entire body as the pulpit minister gave notice of the picnic.
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0016 }

“A shiver ran along my spine, Thirza! Until that moment, I doubt I had truly trusted that a picnic would genuinely take place. I had been terrified that it was merely a figment of my imagination. However, once a minister announces something from the pulpit, you are forced to accept it as real.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0017 }

“Nell, you place far too much importance on things,” Thirza stated, sighing. “I fear that life holds a great number of disappointments for you.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0018 }

“Oh, Thirza, anticipating events accounts for half of their enjoyment,” cried Nell. “The items themselves might elude you; yet you cannot be deprived of the delight of anticipating them. It is stated by Mrs. Sowerby, ‘Blessed are they who expect nothing for they shall not be disappointed.’ However, my belief is that anticipating nothing would prove more unpleasant than experiencing disappointment.”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0019 }

Thirza had put on her amethyst brooch for church that day, just like she always did. To go to church without her amethyst brooch was something Thirza never did. Omitting it would have seemed to her almost blasphemous—just as improper as neglecting to bring her Bible or her collection dime. Thirza prized that amethyst brooch above all her other belongings. It had been presented to her mother by an uncle who was a sailor, and her mother had subsequently left it to Thirza. The piece was a traditional oval shape, housing a woven lock of her mother's hair and framed by an outer ring of exceptionally high-quality amethysts. Because she was unversed in gemology, Thirza failed to appreciate just how exquisite those amethysts truly were; nevertheless, she found them gorgeous and remained delightfully aware of their purple glow resting at her neck, just above her best brown satin gown, despite its being out of her line of sight.
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0020 }

When Nell had initially laid eyes on that brooch, she was struck with thrilled wonder.
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0021 }

“Oh, Thirza, this pin is absolutely exquisite. Having it pinned on would make it impossible for me to focus on the prayers or the sermon, though I have no idea how you manage. I know for a fact I would fail. To me, amethysts are simply charming. They match the image I used to hold of diamonds. Way back, prior to ever laying eyes on a real diamond, I encountered them in a book and attempted to picture their appearance. My expectation was that they were gorgeous, shining violet gems. My disappointment was so great that tears came when I eventually glimpsed an actual diamond set in a woman’s ring. Naturally, its beauty was undeniable, yet it failed to match my vision of a diamond. Would you allow me to have the pin in my hand for just a moment, Thirza? Could amethysts possibly represent the spirits of virtuous violets?”
{: #nw-v01-c13-p0022 }
